summary.headline: Lloyds Metals H1 FY27 record: revenue INR9,545 crore (+94% YoY), EBITDA margin 38.33% (+542 bps), PAT INR2,639 crore (+113%).
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose 62% YoY to INR4,132 crore and EBITDA rose 83% to INR1,538 crore, with a 37.22% margin (+419 bps). Management attributes the margin gains to the slurry pipeline cutting iron ore freight, higher realisations and a richer mix of value-added products such as pellets, which now make up 61% of standalone revenue. Thriveni's Q2 was weaker on monsoon disruption and higher diesel and explosives costs, with pass-through negotiations under way. Management guided to ~INR13,000 crore capex for FY27, and the Chemaf debt restructuring is targeted for closure within 3 to 4 months. Copper FY27 target was cut to 5,850 tonnes from 8,000 tonnes because of Surya Mines feed and sulphuric acid constraints.

segments.name: Iron ore (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 production 3.95 Mt (+15.5% YoY) and sales 2.12 Mt; H1 production 10 Mt (+35%). Realisation ~INR670/t, EBITDA INR2,082/t in Q2 (INR2,239/t H1). Monthly run rate above 2 Mt.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: Q2 DRI sales 160.6 kt (+81% YoY); H1 343.1 kt (+104%). DRI realisation INR31,040/t with EBITDA INR9,231/t in Q2. Power volumes +82% in Q2 and +85% in H1.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Q2 production 2.11 Mt; H1 3.81 Mt after second plant commissioned in May. Realisation INR11,348/t in Q2 (INR11,520/t H1); EBITDA INR4,604/t in Q2 (INR4,988/t H1). Sales mix 71% domestic, 29% export.

segments.name: Thriveni (MDO, mining)
segments.commentary: H1 iron ore volume 30.31 Mt including BHQ and coal 44.84 million cubic metres including overburden. Q2 margins were hit by rain and fuel and explosives costs; management says pass-through is being negotiated with clients.

guidance_outlook: FY27 iron ore volume expected at about 8 Mt, rising to about 9.5 Mt in FY28, as the 20% add-on takes capacity from 8 Mt to 9.6 Mt over the next 3 to 4 months.
Capex guided at about INR13,000 crore for FY27 (H1 INR6,000 crore) and around INR10,000 crore or more in FY28.
Wire rod steel plant: blast furnace and coke oven to start in Q4 FY27, steel plant and wire rod mill in Q1 CY2027, a quarter later than earlier planned.
Beneficiation volumes expected from FY29; usable iron ore stays at 26 Mt through the period.
Chemaf debt restructuring expected to close within 3 to 4 months, before the end of FY27. Long-run Chemaf net debt guided to about $500 million from about $800 million today.
Copper FY27 target cut to 5,850 t from 8,000 t. Chemaf plants targeted for production in FY28.
Management expects H2 volumes to rise in Lloyds Metals and the MDO business, with DRI operations strong. Copper is expected to be slower in H2.
Management indicated about 38% margin for both H1 and H2 at standalone level.
capex_capacity: Pellets: both 4 Mt plants running above rated capacity; debottlenecking under way and a third pellet plant being added.

Steel: 1.2 Mt integrated plant (wire rod) progressing toward commissioning. Separately, a 3 Mt steel plan has 1,200 acres of land and a 4.5 Mt EC; only the captive power plant has started, and the configuration study is due in a couple of months.
Slurry pipeline: first line at full capacity; a longer, larger network is planned to carry beneficiated material.
Chemaf: Etoile and Mutoshi copper-cobalt complexes targeted at 74,000 t copper and 20,000 t cobalt a year at full potential, with completion targeted by FY27 end and production in FY28.

Thriveni: Western Hill has 88 electric units operating and 20 more at the rail siding; 14 mobile crushers and 26 heavy earthmoving units mobilised for BHQ. Gold plan approved for 1.5 Mtpa mining and processing at Thriveni Lloyds Swarnagiri.
demand_pricing: Management says iron ore pricing is set internally based on end-product market, stocks and order book, and sees INR6,700/t as sustainable.
Sulphuric acid shortage in DRC is raising Surya Mines costs; diesel in DRC is about $3.2/litre, roughly 3x India.
Thriveni cost pressure from higher HSD and explosives prices after the West Asia crisis; pass-through to clients under negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is iron ore realisation above benchmark, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific Indian benchmark and that INR6,700/t reflects quality; it believes pricing can sustain. It says 26 Mt of ore is available to 2051, and it is not expanding downstream beyond ore availability.

qa_highlights.question: When will Chemaf debt restructuring complete and what is the net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Closure targeted within 3 to 4 months, before FY27 end. Net debt is guided to about $500 million long-run from about $800 million, including capex debt. Consolidation is full, with 51% of profit going to minority interest.

qa_highlights.question: Thriveni margin dip in Q2 and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the rainy season in Odisha and Jharkhand, plus higher fuel and explosives costs. Pass-through to NTPC-linked mine owners is being implemented, and management does not foresee missing its EBITDA projections.

qa_highlights.question: Tata Steel MDO scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Work is via BRPL, a Tata Steel and Lloyds JV, with equipment rented to it. Expected 12-14 Mt iron ore and 1.5-1.8 Mt manganese from next year; rates not yet final. Joda West manganese began at small scale, with a fuller ramp from December.

qa_highlights.question: Copper FY27 target: 8,000 t on slide 15 or 5,850 t on slide 20?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is now 5,850 t for FY27. The cut reflects Surya Mines challenges and a focus on completing Chemaf. Third-party ore processing is less lucrative, so ramp-up is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Funding: borrowings and debt levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone borrowing plan is about INR9,500 crore, with debt-to-equity targeted at 60-65% (below 75%). Net debt is within 1x to 1.5x forward 12-month EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 weakness and H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is seasonally weak due to monsoon and cost pressure, but management says standalone margins are steady at about 37-38% across H1 and H2. Volumes are expected to rise in H2.

risks_watch: Surya Mines copper output is constrained by sulphuric acid availability and cost, and by third-party ore; FY27 copper target is 5,850 t.
Chemaf restructuring (target 3 to 4 months) and its debt at about $800 million, with minority dilution of 51%.
Steel plant commissioning slipped about a quarter; blast furnace and coke oven start in Q4 FY27.
Thriveni margin pass-through on fuel and explosives costs is still under negotiation.
Chemaf PNG (Panguna) project is at an early stage with no agreement signed and no volume or cost projections.
$300 million NCD enabling resolution in place; use of proceeds not defined beyond capex.
Consolidated net debt below INR20,000 crore, with standalone net debt INR9,316 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on standalone margins and H1 records, and evasive on specifics (Panguna, the copper target and the hypothetical war impact). Management was cautious on Surya Mines and copper near-term execution. Management answered the Q2 seasonality and Thriveni questions with clear explanations.
key_quotes: the first half of FY27 has been the best H1 in the company's history, record revenue, record EBITDA and record PAT on both a stand-alone and a consolidated basis
This is a structural re-rating of the earnings base, not a cyclical spike.
We are not chasing volume for its own sake. We are building a business that is structurally advantaged and built to last.

growth.why: Guidance for FY27 iron ore volume of about 8 Mt (rising to 9.5 Mt in FY28) is backed by the 8 to 9.6 Mt add-on due in 3 to 4 months, pellet plants running above rated capacity and a third pellet plant, plus a wire rod steel plant slipping a quarter; FY27 capex guided at ~INR13,000 crore, but the copper target was cut to 5,850 t and Chemaf production is pushed to FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided standalone margin of about 38% for both H1 and H2, after Q2 at 37.22% (+419 bps YoY), with slurry pipeline cutting freight and pellets at 61% of standalone revenue, though Thriveni pass-through is still under negotiation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 20% add-on takes iron ore capacity from 8 Mt to 9.6 Mt in 3 to 4 months, the Chemaf complexes are under construction for FY28 production, and the wire rod steel plant starts blast furnace in Q4 FY27 and steel/wire rod mill in Q1 CY2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 iron ore volume guided at about 8 Mt against H1 production of 10 Mt (+35%) and a monthly run rate above 2 Mt, with DRI sales up 104% in H1 and H2 volumes expected to rise; copper is the exception, cut to 5,850 t.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is guided at about INR13,000 crore (H1 INR6,052 crore) and about INR10,000 crore or more in FY28, and a 3 Mt steel configuration study is due in a couple of months with 1,200 acres of land already held.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Copper FY27 target was cut from 8,000 t to 5,850 t, Chemaf production is pushed to FY28, and steel commissioning slipped about a quarter, so the guidance direction is mixed rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Copper is already cut and Surya Mines is constrained by sulphuric acid, Thriveni pass-through is unresolved after the Q2 margin hit, and the steel plant slipped a quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The wire rod steel plant (1.2 Mt integrated) starts blast furnace and coke oven in Q4 FY27 and steel plant and wire rod mill in Q1 CY2027, but it has already slipped a quarter and no product volumes are guided.

rows.label: Chemaf debt restructuring closure
rows.why: Management targets closure before FY27 end, with long-run Chemaf net debt guided to about $500 million from about $800 million today.

rows.label: Chemaf copper-cobalt production
rows.why: Etoile and Mutoshi are targeted at 74,000 t copper and 20,000 t cobalt a year at full potential, with completion by FY27 end and production in FY28, but FY27 copper is cut to 5,850 t.

rows.label: Tata Steel MDO scope via BRPL
rows.why: Expected 12-14 Mt iron ore and 1.5-1.8 Mt manganese from next year, but rates are not yet final.

tone.note: Management was confident on standalone margins at about 38% and H1 records, and cautious on Surya Mines, copper execution and Thriveni pass-through; analysts pushed on the iron ore realisation sustainability, the copper target cut and Thriveni's Q2 dip.
